blocks.content: CMD specifies the default command a container runs when it starts, and unlike RUN, it executes at container start time, not at build time.
1. The Default Command at Container Start
blocks.text: 1. The Default Command at Container Start

blocks.content: When a container starts and no command was explicitly given on the docker run line, whatever CMD specifies is what actually executes as the container's main process.

blocks.alt: CMD is what runs when the container actually starts

blocks.content: Anything you type after the image name on a docker run command replaces the Dockerfile's CMD entirely. This makes CMD a convenient default rather than a hard rule.

blocks.alt: Anything typed after the image name replaces CMD

blocks.content:
docker run myapp                 # runs the Dockerfile's CMD
docker run myapp echo "hi"        # runs "echo hi" instead, CMD is ignored

code.content:

docker run myapp echo "hi"        # runs "echo hi" instead, CMD is ignored

codes.bash:
docker run myapp                 # runs the Dockerfile's CMD

blocks.content: It bears repeating clearly since it is a common point of confusion: CMD does not run while the image is being built, it only runs the moment a container starts from that image.

blocks.alt: Nothing about CMD executes during the build itself

blocks.title: Key Takeaway
points: CMD sets the default command a container runs at start time, and it is easily overridden by anything passed to docker run.
Unlike RUN, CMD never executes during the build, only when a container actually starts.
